component.name: Desk Connect
component.summary: Share one keyboard and mouse across two computers over USB-C

description.p: Desk Connect lets you drive a second computer with the keyboard and mouse attached to the first one, using a direct USB-C / Thunderbolt cable instead of Wi-Fi or a network router.

Connect the two machines with a Thunderbolt 3/4 or USB4 cable. Each side gets a private point-to-point network interface; Desk Connect streams input events across it with sub-millisecond latency. Press a hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+S by default) to flip control between the local and remote machine.

ul.li: Works on X11 and Wayland (GNOME and KDE) — injection happens below the compositor via uinput
No internet, Wi-Fi, or router required — traffic stays on the cable
Exclusive device grab so the local session is untouched while you drive the remote
Automatic reconnection if the cable is replugged

description.p: The connection now binds strictly to the cable's link-local address on both ends, so Wi-Fi can never be used, and announcing stops once connected. Touchpads gain tap-to-click, two/three-finger taps and two-finger scroll.
Discovery is now cable-only so traffic never falls back to Wi-Fi, and laptop touchpads work via absolute-to-relative pointer conversion.
Auto-discovery and auto-connect when the cable is plugged in, an on-screen control button, start-at-login, and clearer diagnostics.
First release: server/client roles, USB-C link detection, hotkey switching.
